steps.title: Personal details
steps.purpose: Identify the employee for the pension fund registration and HR correspondence.
steps.intro_text: Let's start with a few details about you.

steps.title: Home address
steps.purpose: Collect the full postal address for HR mail. The country also decides source tax liability, and the canton is needed for the pension fund.
steps.intro_text: Please enter your home address the way you would write it on an envelope. We post documents to this address.

steps.title: Nationality and permit
steps.purpose: Check whether a Swiss resident is subject to source tax. Only asked of people living in Switzerland, because everyone living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality.

steps.title: Start of employment
steps.purpose: Confirm the first working day. The pension fund insurance start date is derived from it.
steps.intro_text: Please confirm your first working day.

steps.title: Civil status and spouse
steps.purpose: Collect the civil status and spouse's date of birth for the pension fund, and spouse details that can exempt a married employee from source tax.
steps.intro_text: The pension fund needs your civil status. If you are married, we also need some details about your spouse.

steps.title: Source tax details
steps.purpose: Collect the inputs for the Zurich source tax tariff calculator. Only shown to employees who are subject to source tax.
steps.intro_text: You are subject to source tax. We need a few more details to determine your tax tariff.

fields.label: First name
fields.question: What is your first name?
fields.help_text: As shown on your passport or ID card.
validation: required non-empty after trimming whitespace
fields.notes: Required by the pension portal. HR's need for the name for addressing post is inferred from F-TR-010.

fields.label: Last name
fields.question: What is your last name?
fields.help_text: As shown on your passport or ID card.
validation: required non-empty after trimming whitespace
fields.notes: HR consumer is inferred, as for first_name.

fields.label: Date of birth
fields.question: What is your date of birth?
validation: must be a valid calendar date
must not be in the future

fields.label: Street
fields.question: What street do you live on?
validation: required non-empty after trimming whitespace

fields.label: House number
fields.question: What is your house number?
validation: required non-empty after trimming whitespace
free text (allows e.g. '12a')

fields.label: Postcode
fields.question: What is your postcode?
validation: required non-empty after trimming whitespace
free text; no country-specific format check (none given by the sources)

fields.label: Town
fields.question: What town do you live in?
validation: required non-empty after trimming whitespace

fields.label: Country
fields.question: In which country do you live?
fields.help_text: The country of your home address. If you live outside Switzerland (for example, you commute across the border), choose that country.
validation: must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code

consumers.purpose: Country of residence: anyone living outside CH is always subject to source tax

fields.notes: Also serves as the residence country, so the employee is asked once (see OQ-07). The id residence_country is deliberately not used as a separate field.

fields.label: Canton
fields.question: In which canton do you live?
validation: must be one of the 26 option values
fields.notes: Option values are the official two-letter canton abbreviations; labels match the portal exactly. Only asked of Swiss residents because the portal lists only Swiss cantons. What the fund needs for residents abroad, and whether 'Canton' means residence canton or work canton, is unresolved (OQ-03).

fields.label: Nationality
fields.question: What is your nationality?
fields.help_text: If you have more than one nationality and one of them is Swiss, choose Switzerland.
validation: must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code

consumers.purpose: Liability check: Swiss nationals living in CH are not subject to source tax

fields.notes: Not asked of residents abroad, because they are subject regardless of nationality (F-TR-037). Whether the calculator itself needs nationality is open (OQ-01). The dual-nationality help text rests on 'If you don't have a Swiss passport'.

fields.label: Residence permit
fields.question: Which Swiss residence permit do you have?
fields.help_text: Choose the permit type shown on your permit card. A C permit means a settlement permit.
validation: must be one of the option values

consumers.purpose: Liability check: C permit holders are not subject to source tax
First-day logistics: remind the employee to bring the permit

fields.notes: Only B and C appear in the sources. 'other' covers everything else until the calculator's permit list is known (OQ-06).

fields.label: First working day
fields.question: What is your first working day at Muster AG?
fields.help_text: Please check this date carefully. If it changes, for example because you agree an earlier exit with your current employer, update it here straight away. The pension fund insurance start depends on it.
validation: must be a valid calendar date

consumers.purpose: Basis for the derived insurance start date

fields.label: Civil status
fields.question: What is your civil status?
validation: must be one of the option values

consumers.purpose: Married employees may be exempt via their spouse; it also changes the calculator's questions

fields.notes: The options are exactly the portal's four (G-07). Registered partnership is not supported by the portal (OQ-04).

fields.label: Spouse's date of birth
fields.question: What is your spouse's date of birth?
validation: must be a valid calendar date
must not be in the future

consumers.purpose: BVG registration (required when civil status is Married)

fields.label: Spouse's nationality
fields.question: What is your spouse's nationality?
fields.help_text: If your spouse has more than one nationality and one of them is Swiss, choose Switzerland.
validation: must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
fields.ask_when: civil_status == "married" and address_country == "CH" and nationality != "CH" and permit_type != "C"

consumers.purpose: Spouse exemption: married to a Swiss national who lives in CH means no source tax

fields.notes: Only asked when the spouse exemption could change the outcome (F-TR-044).

fields.label: Spouse's residence permit
fields.question: Which Swiss residence permit does your spouse have?
fields.help_text: Choose 'Other permit / no permit' if your spouse has no Swiss permit, for example because they live abroad.
validation: must be one of the option values
fields.ask_when: civil_status == "married" and address_country == "CH" and nationality != "CH" and permit_type != "C" and spouse_nationality != "CH"

consumers.purpose: Spouse exemption: married to a C permit holder who lives in CH means no source tax

fields.notes: Uses the same option set as permit_type (OQ-06).

fields.label: Spouse's country of residence
fields.question: In which country does your spouse live?
validation: must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
fields.ask_when: civil_status == "married" and address_country == "CH" and nationality != "CH" and permit_type != "C" and (spouse_nationality == "CH" or spouse_permit_type == "C")

consumers.purpose: Spouse exemption applies only if the spouse lives in CH

fields.notes: Only relevant when the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit. 'Lives here' is interpreted as CH (F-TR-045).

fields.label: Spouse works
fields.question: Does your spouse work (is your spouse gainfully employed)?
validation: must be answered yes or no

consumers.purpose: Input to the Zurich tariff calculator for married employees

fields.notes: Only the transcript supports this; the calculator source has no extracted facts yet (OQ-01). The calculator's exact wording and options are unknown.

rules.description: Whether the employee is subject to source tax. Residents abroad are always subject. Residents of CH are not subject if they are Swiss, hold a C permit, or are married to a Swiss national or C permit holder who lives in CH. Everyone else is subject.
rules.expression: address_country != "CH" or (address_country == "CH" and nationality != "CH" and permit_type != "C" and not (civil_status == "married" and (spouse_nationality == "CH" or spouse_permit_type == "C") and spouse_residence_country == "CH"))

consumers.purpose: Decides whether a tariff must be determined at all

rules.description: Pension fund insurance start: the first working day if it is the 1st of a month, otherwise the 1st of the following month.

consumers.purpose: BVG registration (required, DD.MM.YYYY, must be the 1st of a month)

notices.text: Please bring your residence permit with you on your first working day.
Your pension fund insurance starts on the 1st of the month on or after your first working day. If your start date changes, please update it here right away.

open_questions.question: Which questions does the Zurich source tax calculator ask to determine the tariff code (including the extra questions and German forms for residents abroad), with their options and conditions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No facts were extracted from the calculator source. The source tax step currently holds only 'spouse works' (from the transcript). Without the calculator's questions, Lonio cannot collect enough to determine the tariff.
options: Extract the calculator facts and extend the source_tax step
Ship liability determination only; HR collects the tariff inputs manually
open_questions.recommendation: Extract the calculator's questions before building the source_tax step. The liability rule and the other steps can be built now.

open_questions.question: What should be entered in the pension portal's required 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean the residence canton or the work canton?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The dropdown lists only Swiss cantons, and the field is required. Cross-border employees exist (Konstanz, Liechtenstein). If it means the work canton, the employee should not be asked at all.
options: Residence canton; ask only Swiss residents; ask the fund what to use for residents abroad
Work canton; do not ask the employee; HR/employer supplies it (e.g. Zurich)
Ask everyone abroad for a canton
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster. Until then, ask only Swiss residents for their residence canton and flag registrations of residents abroad for HR.

open_questions.question: How should employees in a registered partnership (or with other statuses such as separated) be recorded, and does the fund want the partner's date of birth?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Such an employee exists (Daniel), but the portal offers only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed. Adding an option the fund does not support would break the registration.
options: Keep the four portal options; HR handles partnerships manually
Add 'registered_partnership' and map it per the fund's answer; ask partner's date of birth if required
Treat registered partnership as married
open_questions.recommendation: Keep the four portal options for now and ask the fund. Add a 'registered_partnership' option once its mapping and partner-data requirements are known.

open_questions.question: Is the source tax liability rule complete? Anna ended with 'I think that's it'.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Any missing exemption or condition would wrongly show or hide the source tax questions.
options: Confirm the rule as specified
Add missing conditions
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR and cross-check against the calculator.

open_questions.question: Is 'Spouse's date of birth' hidden in the portal for Divorced and Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No screenshot shows these states. The spec asks for the spouse's date of birth only when the employee is married.
options: Only for Married (as specified)
Also for divorced/widowed
open_questions.recommendation: Keep 'only married' (consistent with the transcript) and verify in the portal.

open_questions.question: Which permit types must the permit fields offer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The sources name only B and C. The calculator may need to distinguish other permits.
options: B, C, other (as specified)
The full permit list from the calculator
open_questions.recommendation: Keep B / C / other until the calculator facts are extracted.

open_questions.question: Is the postal address always the residence address, so that address_country can serve as the residence country?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Liability depends on the country of residence. A different mailing address would give the wrong result.
options: Yes, one address (as specified)
Ask for the residence country separately
open_questions.recommendation: Use one address. Anna described a normal home address.

open_questions.question: What exact wording should the permit reminder use, and when should it be shown?
options: Use the drafted wording
HR provides the wording
open_questions.recommendation: Use the draft and let HR review it.

open_questions.question: Are there limits on dates (e.g. first working day not in the past, or a maximum distance in the future) and how does the portal word date errors?
options: Validate only as a calendar date (as specified)
Add range limits
open_questions.recommendation: Validate as a calendar date only, until HR or the fund defines limits.
